source_text: Immo, inquit, praeceptum adimplevit fugiens de civitate in civitatem. Sic enim voluit quidam, sed et ipse fugitivus, argumentari, et qui proinde nolunt intellegere sensum domini illius pronuntiationis, ut eam ad velamentum timiditatis suae utantur, cum et personas suas habuerit et tempora et causas. Cum coeperint, inquit, persequi vos, fugite de civitate in civitatem. Hoc in personas proprie apostolorum et in tempora et in causas eorum pertinere defendimus, sicut subsequentes sensus probabunt, qui non nisi in apostolos competunt: In viam nationum ne ieritis et in civitatem Samaritanorum ne introieritis, sed ite potius ad oves perditas domus Israëlis. Nobis autem et via nationum patet, in qua et inventi sumus et usque in finem incedimus, et nulla civitas excepta est, quo per totum orbem praedicamus, sed nec cura nobis Israëlis iniuncta est extra ordinem, nisi qua et omnibus gentibus praedicare debemus. Etiam si apprehendamur, non in concilia eorum perducemur nec in synagogis illorum flagellabimur, sed Romanis utique potestatibus et tribunalibus obiciemur. Sic igitur et fugae praeceptum apostolorum condicio desiderabat, quoniam primo praedicandum erat ad oves perditas domus Israëlis. Ut ergo perficeretur praedicatio apud quos priores eam perfici oportebat, uti panem ante filii quam canes sumerent, ideo illis fugere tunc ad tempus praecepti, non propter eludendum periculum proprio nomine persecutionis (atquin persecutiones eos passuros praedicabat et tolerandas docebat), sed propter profectum annuntiationis, ne statim oppressis evangelii quoque disseminatio perimeretur. Neque enim quasi tacite in aliquam civitatem transfugiendum erat, sed quasi ubique annuntiaturis et ex hoc ubique persecutiones subituris, donec replerent doctrinam suam. Denique, Non consummabitis, inquit, civitates Israëlis. Adeo intra terminos Iudaeae praeceptum fugae continebatur. Nobis autem nulla Iudaeae praefinitio competit praedicationis in omnem iam carnem effuso spiritu sancto. Itaque Paulus et apostoli ipsi memores praecepti dominici contestantur illud apud Israël, quem iam doctrina sua impleverant, Vobis oportuit in primis sermonem dei tradi, sed quoniam repulistis eum nec dignos vos aeterna vita existimastis, ecce convertimus nos ad nationes. Atque exinde conversi et ipsi, sicut antecessores instituerant, et in viam nationum abierunt et in civitates Samaritanorum introierunt, ut in totam scilicet terram exiret sonus eorum et in terminos orbis voces eorum. Si ergo cessavit exceptio viae nationum et introitus in civitates Samaritanorum, cur non cessaverit et fugae praeceptum pariter emissum? Denique ex quo saturato Israële apostoli in nationes transierunt, nec fugerunt de civitate in civitatem nec pati dubitaverunt. Atquin et Paulus, qui se per murum concesserat expediri de persecutione, qua ad hoc tempus erat praecepti, idem iam in clausula officii et in consummatione praecepti discipulis magnopere deprecantibus, ne se Hierosolvma committeret passurus illic quae Agabus prophetaverat, sollicitudini eorum non subscripsit, sed e contrario, Quid, inquit, facitis lacrimantes et conturbantes cor meum? Ego enim non modo vincula pati optaverim, sed etiam mori Hierosolymis pro nomine domini mei Iesu Christi. Atque ita omnes aierunt, Fiat voluntas domini. Quae erat voluntas domini? Utique non fugiendi iam persecutionem. Ceterum poterant et priorem domini voluntatem proposuisse, qua fugere mandaverat, qui illum persecutionem vitasse maluerant. Igitur cum etiam sub apostolis ipsis temporale fuerit fugae praeceptum, sicut et reliquorum praescriptorum, non potest apud nos perseverare, quod apud doctores nostros concessavit, etsi non proprie ad illos fuisset emissum, aut, si perseverare illud dominus voluit, deliquerunt apostoli, qui non usque in finem fugere curaverunt.
thought_title: The flight command was only for the apostles, for a limited time
orientation: Tertullian is answering the objection that the Lord's command to flee from city to city still applies to Christians.
pass_a_gloss: On the contrary, he says, he fulfilled the command by fleeing from city to city. For so a certain man wanted to argue, but he himself was also a fugitive, and those who therefore do not want to understand the meaning of that pronouncement of the Lord, so that they use it as a covering for their own cowardice, since it had its own persons and times and causes. When they begin, he says, to persecute you, flee from city to city. We maintain that this pertains properly to the persons of the apostles and to their times and causes, as the following meanings will prove, which fit no one but the apostles: Do not go into the way of the nations and do not enter into a city of the Samaritans, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. But to us the way of the nations is open, in which we were also found and in which we walk even to the end, and no city is excepted, where we preach throughout the whole world, but nor has care of Israel been enjoined on us outside the order, except in which we ought to preach also to all nations. Even if we are seized, we will not be led into their councils nor will we be scourged in their synagogues, but we will certainly be brought before Roman powers and tribunals. So therefore the condition of the apostles also required the command of flight, since first it was necessary to preach to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. So that therefore the preaching might be completed among those among whom it was necessary for it to be completed first, so that the children might take bread before the dogs, for that reason it was commanded to them to flee then for a time, not for the sake of evading danger under the proper name of persecution (but rather he was foretelling that they would suffer persecutions and was teaching that they must be endured), but for the sake of the progress of the announcement, lest when they were immediately crushed the dissemination of the gospel also be destroyed. For it was not necessary to flee over into some city as if silently, but as those who were about to announce everywhere and from this about to undergo persecutions everywhere, until they should fill up their teaching. Finally, You will not finish, he says, the cities of Israel. So much was the command of flight contained within the boundaries of Judea. But to us no limitation of Judea applies for preaching, since the Holy Spirit has now been poured out upon all flesh. And so Paul and the apostles themselves, mindful of the Lord's command, testify to that among Israel, whom they had already filled with their teaching, It was necessary for the word of God to be delivered to you first, but since you have rejected it and have not judged yourselves worthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the nations. And from then on, having turned, they themselves, as their predecessors had established, both went into the way of the nations and entered into the cities of the Samaritans, so that, of course, their sound might go out into all the earth and their words into the ends of the world. If therefore the exception of the way of the nations and the entrance into the cities of the Samaritans has ceased, why should not the command of flight, issued equally, also have ceased? Finally, from the time when Israel was filled and the apostles passed over to the nations, they neither fled from city to city nor hesitated to suffer. But indeed also Paul, who had allowed himself to be let down through the wall to be freed from the persecution, which was for this time of the command, the same man now at the close of his office and in the completion of the command, when his disciples were earnestly begging him not to commit himself to Jerusalem, about to suffer there what Agabus had prophesied, did not subscribe to their anxiety, but on the contrary, Why, he says, do you act weeping and troubling my heart? For I would wish not only to suffer chains, but even to die at Jerusalem for the name of my Lord Jesus Christ. And so all said, Let the will of the Lord be done. What was the will of the Lord? Certainly no longer to flee persecution. Otherwise they could have set forth the earlier will of the Lord, by which he had commanded flight, those who had preferred that he avoid persecution. Therefore since even under the apostles themselves the command of flight was temporary, just as also of the other prescriptions, it cannot persist among us, what ceased among our teachers, even if it had not been issued properly to them, or, if the Lord willed it to persist, the apostles erred, who did not take care to flee even to the end.

pass_b_english: But, someone says, he fulfilled the command by fleeing from city to city. That is how a certain man wanted to argue, himself also a fugitive, and there are those who refuse to understand the meaning of the Lord's pronouncement so that they can use it as a covering for their own cowardice, even though it had its own persons, times, and reasons.

When they begin to persecute you, he says, flee from city to city (Matthew 10:23). We maintain that this pertains specifically to the persons of the apostles, and to their times and reasons, as the words that follow will prove, since they fit no one but the apostles: Do not go in the way of the nations, and do not enter a city of the Samaritans, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel (Matthew 10:5-6).

But for us the way of the nations lies open. In it we were found, and in it we walk to the end. No city is excluded, since we preach throughout the whole world. Nor has the care of Israel been laid upon us as a special charge, except insofar as we must preach to all nations. Even if we are arrested, we will not be led into their councils or flogged in their synagogues; we will be handed over to Roman authorities and tribunals.

So the condition of the apostles required the command to flee, because the gospel had first to be preached to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. In order that the preaching might be completed among those to whom it had to be completed first, so that the children might take the bread before the dogs, they were commanded to flee at that time. This was not to evade danger under the name of persecution. Indeed he foretold that they would suffer persecutions and taught that they must be endured. Rather, it was for the progress of the announcement, so that the dissemination of the gospel might not be destroyed if they were immediately crushed.

For they were not to flee secretly into some city, but as men who would announce the gospel everywhere and therefore undergo persecutions everywhere, until they had filled up their teaching. Finally, he says, You will not finish the cities of Israel (Matthew 10:23). So the command to flee was confined within the borders of Judea.

But for us no boundary of Judea applies to our preaching, since the Holy Spirit has now been poured out upon all flesh. Thus Paul and the apostles themselves, mindful of the Lord's command, testify to Israel, whom they had already filled with their teaching: It was necessary that the word of God be delivered to you first, but since you have rejected it and judged yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the nations (Acts 13:46).

And from then on they turned, as they themselves had previously established, and went into the way of the nations and entered the cities of the Samaritans, so that their sound went out into all the earth and their words to the ends of the world (Psalm 19:4). If, then, the exception of the way of the nations and the entrance into the cities of the Samaritans has ceased, why should not the command to flee, which was issued together with it, also have ceased?

Finally, from the time when Israel was filled and the apostles passed over to the nations, they neither fled from city to city nor hesitated to suffer. Indeed Paul, who had let himself be lowered through the wall to escape the persecution that belonged to that time of the command, later, at the close of his ministry and the completion of the command, when the disciples earnestly begged him not to go to Jerusalem to suffer there what Agabus had foretold, did not subscribe to their anxiety.

On the contrary, he said, What are you doing, weeping and troubling my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound but even to die in Jerusalem for the name of my Lord Jesus Christ (Acts 21:13). And so they all said, Let the will of the Lord be done (Acts 21:14).

What was the will of the Lord? Surely no longer to flee persecution. Otherwise they could have set before him the earlier will of the Lord, by which he had commanded flight, those who preferred that he avoid persecution.

Therefore, since even under the apostles themselves the command to flee was temporary, like the rest of their instructions, what ceased among our teachers cannot continue among us, even if it had not been issued specifically to them. Or, if the Lord willed it to continue, the apostles sinned, who did not take care to flee to the end.

fixed: Changed 'as their predecessors had established' to 'as they themselves had previously established' to clarify that the apostles followed their own earlier practice, not some unnamed predecessors.

The Matthew 15:26 citation is a paraphrase of the source's 'uti panem ante filii quam canes sumerent' (so that the children might take bread before the dogs), not a direct quote of Matthew 15:26; the English accurately renders the source's paraphrase, so no edit was made.
